query: What are the common advantage attributes of airlines whose overall rating is high?

per_column.name: crew_service_quality
per_column.rationale: A graded categorical read of crew service is a strong axis for identifying advantage attributes tied to high ratings. Samples map soundly ('outstanding', 'consistently good', 'very nice and helpful' -> exceptional/good). Slightly generous readings but well grounded.

per_column.name: crew_above_and_beyond
per_column.rationale: Distinguishes extraordinary effort from baseline good service, a plausible new axis. However sample 1 marks True where the text describes good but arguably routine service; the flag is somewhat subjective and one reading overreaches. Mostly defensible.

per_column.name: personalized_service
per_column.rationale: Potentially useful axis, but grounding is shaky: sample 5 ('cabin crew nice and helpful') is marked True for personalization without clear individualized-service evidence, and sample 1's True is a stretch. Several inferences exceed the text.

per_column.name: service_consistency
per_column.rationale: Consistency is a meaningful attribute for high-rating airlines. Grounded where text says 'consistently good from start to finish'; other rows are inferred but reasonable. Some rows lack explicit consistency cues, mildly speculative.

per_column.name: food_quality
per_column.rationale: Graded food read is a clear analytical axis and maps well to text ('very high quality', 'excellent', 'plentiful'). NULLs for silent rows are appropriate. Well grounded.

per_column.name: seat_comfort_perception
per_column.rationale: Adds a qualitative seat dimension beyond the numeric Seat Comfort column, distinguishing flat-bed vs upright vs cramped. Samples align ('spacious and comfortable' -> spacious_upright, 'lie down bed' -> spacious_flat_bed). Well grounded.

per_column.name: ife_quality
per_column.rationale: Useful axis distinct from the raw Inflight Entertainment column. Mostly grounded, but sample 1 and 5 are marked not_present while text is simply silent (should arguably be NULL), and sample 2 'wide range of movies' -> good is correct. Minor mislabeling of silence as absence.

per_column.name: amenity_provision
per_column.rationale: Captures amenity/service proactivity, a plausible advantage attribute. Uses Unknown/NULL for silent rows appropriately. Some 'proactively_offered' inferences (sample 1) are reasonable from described drink rounds. Moderately grounded.

judge.rationale: The added columns collectively provide genuine, distinct qualitative axes (crew, food, seat, IFE, amenities, consistency) that directly support identifying advantage attributes of high-rated airlines, going beyond the existing numeric ratings. Most values are sound readings of the source text, with appropriate NULL/Unknown handling for silent rows. Groundedness is reduced by a few overreaching inferences in the more subjective boolean columns (crew_above_and_beyond, personalized_service) and by labeling silence as 'not_present' in ife_quality rather than unknown. No column is near-constant or trivially redundant enough to fail on usefulness.
